candidates.demonstrated_gap: writing-for-agents is a general reference for writing anything an agent reads (context pointers, the two loads, pruning principles). Its description also fires on skill edits, which is the manifest's trial confound, and it has no procedure specific to AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. writing-agents-md is scoped to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md only: its 269-char description has no skill-edit trigger, which removes the confound. It adds four things: (1) discovery of the active instruction chain on both hosts (Codex: root to working directory, AGENTS.override.md, 32 KiB limit; Claude Code: ancestor CLAUDE.md files, the context cost of @import, path-scoped rules); (2) a per-rule routing ledger (Keep/Narrow/Defer/Enforce/Delete/Verify), where checklist.md says to 'Record exactly one action and its destination for each rule so no candidate disappears between review and rewrite', which is the overturn metric 'keep every canonical rule'; (3) 'Edit only destinations authorized by the request' and 'Keep one source of truth'; (4) an @AGENTS.md import (a symlink only when there are no Claude-specific additions), which matches this repo's CLAUDE.md layout. It makes no approval step mandatory for bounded work (a review stays read-only unless the user asks for changes), it has no scripts, and it ships evals/evals.json. Risks: a single maintainer and 0 stars (not evidence either way). host-semantics.md still says Claude Code does not natively read AGENTS.md, which is out of date since v2.1.277 per the official docs but harmless for a repo that keeps a CLAUDE.md. candidates.demonstrated_gap: Codex lane only. security-best-practices is the kept winner for secure-coding review of scripts/ and tools/. It is pinned to openai/skills@49f948f, and the README at that same pin says 'This repository is deprecated' (commit 778b0e6, 2026-06-22). That main branch has had no commit since 2026-06-24, and openai/plugins contains no successor folder for it. security-scan runs a 'standard, single-pass security audit of an entire repository or a scoped path', so scripts/ and tools/ can each be audited as a scoped path. It must write three canonical files: scan-manifest.json, findings.json (with severity and confidence levels) and coverage.json. The coverage.json schema fixes completeness as complete, partial or unknown, gives every surface a disposition (reported, no_issue_found, rejected, not_applicable or needs_follow_up), and lists deferred items and explicit exclusions. That amounts to the layer's coverage ledger and a verdict set that maps onto confirmed/needs_validation/rejected. security-best-practices has neither and calls itself 'not a full security audit'. Finalization also writes report.md and SARIF 2.1.0. The skill additionally competes with security-audit (trial) for the whole-repository audit. Preconditions, which are not refutations: (1) It is Codex-only: it calls plugin MCP tools, uses $skill references and ../../references paths, and installs as one 15-skill plugin. It therefore cannot meet the layer's 'in Claude Code and in Codex' rule, and the Claude side needs a cross-client replacement. (2) The docs say 'Running scans requires Codex Security access', and full-repository scans may also need Trusted Access for Cyber. Whether this account has either is unknown; the plugin's advisory Daybreak check at the first preflight establishes it. (3) In non-interactive sessions, config-preflight.md L79 auto-applies config patches. This profile has only warn requirements, so the edit should not trigger, but that is untested; run the trial in a scratch CODEX_HOME. (4) The MCP server is an opaque brotli-compressed bundle from a private upstream that declares itself 'Proprietary'.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: skill-creator paired benchmark, in Codex only because the skill cannot run in Claude Code. Arms: with_skill = codex-security@security-scan (plugin 0.1.24 at 5fd93af, scratch CODEX_HOME, scoped to scripts/ and tools/, plus one repository-mode run); old_skill = a snapshot of security-best-practices at openai/skills@49f948f; a second old_skill arm, security-audit at c1c8a8c1, for repository mode. All runs are spawned in the same turn. Frozen set: copies of scripts/ and tools/ with seeded vulnerabilities (known true positives) and benign security-looking decoys (known false positives). Grader assertions: each seeded bug is reported; no decoy is reported; every in-scope file is accounted for in coverage.json; each verdict maps to confirmed/needs_validation/rejected. Metric: aggregate_benchmark pass_rate, time and tokens (mean +- stddev, delta). Decision rule: adopt for the Codex lane only if pass_rate exceeds both old_skill arms by more than one stddev at no higher token or time cost. If the first preflight's Daybreak advisory returns not_granted or scan outputs are withheld, record the arm as blocked and drop the label to keep_but_compare.

Codex Security's own pull-request review runs in the cloud, while security-diff-scan is the local plugin path. It reviews every changed file of a PR, commit, branch diff or working-tree patch, deleted files included. It runs $threat-model, then $finding-discovery in compact diff mode, then $validation, then $attack-path-analysis. It is labeled keep_but_compare rather than targeted for three reasons: it is narrower (per-PR) than security-scan; the Claude side already has native /security-review plus the round-1 getsentry security-review; and it shares security-scan's preconditions (Codex-only, unknown Codex Security access, an untested auto-remediation boundary, an opaque MCP bundle). counts.trading_layers_note: trading_layers counts only taxonomy layers with at least one selected entry, unlike foundation_layers (which counts every row); trading[] itself always has one row per taxonomy id, so len(manifest["trading"]) can exceed trading_layers whenever a taxonomy layer happens to have zero selected entries
counts.pin_status_note: pins_behind_upstream counts the generator's computed pin fields; pins_behind_upstream_by_review_status splits those rows by published review_status. A row's review_status is pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] only when its computed pin_behind_upstream is true, so review_status_pin_behind_upstream equals the pin_behind_upstream[_unverified] share of that split; a lane pin claim the computed fields contradict is published as pin_status_disputed[_unverified] (the lane's claim in disputed_lane_status and the row evidence) or, on an OS-package pin, distro_managed
counts.pins_behind_note: components with a commit-pinned version (a parenthetical hash), a non-GitHub repository, or an OS-distribution package pin (matched by an -Nubuntu/-Ndeb/+debN pin suffix, or by id via --os-package-ids, e.g. systemd even though its own repository is on GitHub) are excluded from the pin-vs-upstream comparison rather than counted either way
counts.pins_not_compared_note: rows whose pin the generator could not compare with upstream (the exclusions above, plus a pin or upstream latest with no parseable version, reason unversioned) carry pin_behind_upstream null and pin_comparison not_compared, never a definite false
counts.lane_groupings_note: every foundation/trading-scoped count above (candidates_total, candidates_by_disposition, components_confirmed, pins_behind_upstream, pins_behind_upstream_unique_components) is computed from all_rows = manifest['foundation'] + manifest['trading'] only, and so excludes lane_groupings[].selected rows the same way it excludes lane_groupings[].candidates; candidates inside lane_groupings (a review-lane grouping id outside the foundation/taxonomy baseline, e.g. an awesome-list survey) are counted only in lane_grouping_candidates; counts.citation_review (computed below, by apply_citation_review) is the same way scoped -- its rows_flagged/attached only ever count a foundation/trading row, never a lane_groupings[].selected row, since apply_citation_review only walks manifest['foundation'] and manifest['trading']
